purpose: Test strategic generalization after native selection. All twelve seasons and their common tournament finished before these three hand-authored timing opponents were written. They do not enter training, the joint native selection or the original confirmation. Keep this evaluation separate from both the fixed-field confirmation and real elite humans.
styles: A hit selector delays first contact then schedules close recoil clicks. An edge pivot drives toward center with lateral input and changes sprint under contact pressure. A two-beat fighter modulates click admission and strafe with a recurrent oscillator coupled to local hurt timing. Author fixed weights directly in the existing portable inference format, before playing any selected candidate against them.
adaptive_challenge: After the native winner is frozen, train separate MLP and recurrent adversaries explicitly to beat it, on the original 16 training calendars only. Use fresh search seeds, native-legal inputs, phase-shifted openings and unshifted regulation. Select the adversary most successful at ring-outs against the target on the eight original development donors, then average against W-tap and Hold-W as tie-break. This adversary is intentionally informed about the tested bot. Its performance measures exploitability; it is not a blinded human or a representative player.
native_and_sim: Freeze all four opponents, then collect eight new W-tap mirrors. Play the already chosen entry, W-tap, Hold-W and population reference against each under MMC, at 0/0 and 80/80 ms, both seats, four independent native repetitions. Deduplicate repeated candidate identities. Score native ring-outs and draws, both seats and both RTTs. Keep the originally frozen champion through this test.
